title: Why do we hiccup?
examples: Teacher, why do I make a little noise when I hiccup?
Does eating too much make you hiccup?
Is hiccupping bad for my body?

explain.say: A hiccup is a little sound you make when you breathe out quickly.
When you hiccup, a big muscle under your lungs jumps suddenly.
This jumping muscle is called the diaphragm, and it is very important for breathing.
Another thing that happens is that your voice box snaps shut very fast.
When the diaphragm jumps and the cords snap, that makes the little 'hic' sound.
Sometimes, eating too fast or drinking fizzy drinks can make your diaphragm jump.

faq.q: Why do I hiccup? Is it always because of food?
faq.a: Hiccups happen when the diaphragm jumps and the vocal cords snap. Sometimes it is from food, but sometimes it is just from excitement.
asks: Is food the only reason for hiccups?

faq.a: No, hiccups are just little sounds and they do not hurt your body at all. They are just a funny little reflex.

faq.q: How can I stop hiccups if I have many?
faq.a: You can try holding your breath for a little while, or drinking some water slowly. These things can help calm the diaphragm.
asks: What should I do when I hiccup?

faq.a: The diaphragm is a large, important muscle located right under your lungs. It helps you breathe in and out.
Vocal cords are two small bands of tissue inside your voice box. They vibrate when you talk or make sounds.

facts: The diaphragm is a major muscle in the chest.
Hiccups are caused by sudden spasms of the diaphragm.
The snapping of the vocal cords creates the 'hic' sound.

quiz.say: The sudden jump of which muscle causes a hiccup?
quiz.why: The diaphragm is the muscle that jumps, causing the hiccup.

wrong.0: The lungs are where air goes, not the muscle that jumps.
wrong.1: The ribs help you breathe, but they are not the main muscle that spasms.
wrong.3: The vocal cords snap, but the diaphragm jumps first.

quiz.say: What two things happen together to make the hiccup sound?
quiz.show: Diaphragm jump and vocal cord snap

options.show: Diaphragm jump and vocal cord snap
options.say: Diaphragm jump and vocal cord snap

quiz.why: Both the muscle jumping and the cords snapping create the sound.

wrong.1: The snapping of the vocal cords is also needed for the sound.
wrong.2: The diaphragm jump is the main action that starts it.
wrong.3: Drinking water helps stop it, but it does not cause the sound.

quiz.say: If you eat very quickly, what might happen to your breathing muscles?

options.show: You will get a stomach ache
options.say: You will get a stomach ache

quiz.why: Eating too fast can irritate the diaphragm and make it jump.

wrong.0: Stomach aches can happen, but the hiccup is related to breathing muscles.
wrong.1: Hoarseness is from the cords, not the initial hiccup cause.
wrong.2: Falling asleep is different from the muscle twitching.
